properties.evidence: Read from `score_tool` and `term_weights` in service.rs: a term scores +2.0×weight if `desc.contains(term)` — a SUBSTRING match, so "in", "is", "cap" match almost every description; the IDF is `ln(1 + n/df)` with df counted by the same substring rule, so a stopword present in all 180 descriptions still carries weight ln(2)=0.69 rather than zero; and no score is normalised for description length, so a 1,500-char description accumulates matches a 200-char one cannot. Reproduced in Python (164/180 ranks agree with the live server) and ablated one factor at a time: whole-word matching alone changes nothing (56→60 misses), dropping stopwords 56→45, length-normalising 56→43, all three together 56→39. The remaining 12 misses have zero content-word overlap with the tool's name, description or parameters, which no scoring change can reach.
